instruction: Save the currently open blog pages as PDF files to the /home/user/Downloads folder, using the page titles as filenames.

metadata.explanation: Task requires saving two open blog pages as PDFs to Downloads folder. Evaluator checks that at least 2 PDF files exist in the directory. Similar to original but uses a simpler directory structure.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Instruction explicitly requires 'using the page titles as filenames', but evaluator does not verify this requirement at all
The evaluator only checks if at least 2 PDF files exist in /home/user/Downloads, but does not verify filenames match page titles
Expected page titles from URLs are: 'LLM Powered Autonomous Agents' (2023-06-23-agent) and 'Human Data Quality Matters' (2024-02-05-human-data-quality), but no keyword validation is performed
Weak verification: Evaluator accepts ANY 2 PDF files in the directory, even pre-existing or unrelated files
No verification that the PDFs were actually created by the task execution vs pre-existing files
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add required_keywords to match expected page titles: ['agent', 'LLM', 'Autonomous'] and ['human', 'data', 'quality'] or similar variations
Better approach: Extract page titles from the URLs in config and add them to required_keywords for validation
Consider using timestamp-based verification to ensure PDFs are newly created (not pre-existing)
The getter could optionally return file metadata (creation time, size) to enable better verification
Alternatively, verify PDF content matches the blog page URLs to ensure correct pages were saved
